category: Battery Design Module: Battery Interfaces, Aging & Thermal
description: Battery interfaces of the Battery Design Module (Lithium-Ion Battery P2D/DFN and single-ion conductor, Battery with Binary Electrolyte, Lead-Acid, Lumped Battery, Battery Equivalent Circuit, Battery Pack) with their electrode, particle, SOC, cycling, aging, abuse and thermal features. Java type strings and property names come from COMSOL 6.4 Application Library models.

tools.name: Lithium-Ion Battery, Single-Ion Conductor (liion)
tools.description: Model Wizard entry of the Lithium-Ion Battery interface that uses the single-ion conductor charge balance: all electrolyte charge is carried by Li+ ions at constant concentration, so only the electrolyte potential is solved (no salt concentration). It is intended for solid electrolytes or electrolytes whose conductivity does not change with ion transport, and it reduces the computational load compared with the default binary 1:1 liquid electrolyte (concentrated solution theory).
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Batteries > Lithium-Ion Battery, Single-Ion Conductor; Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("liion", "LithiumIonBatteryMPH", "geom1"); model.component("comp1").physics("liion").prop("ElectrolyteType").set("ElectrolyteType", "SingleIonConductor")

parameters.name: prop("ElectrolyteType") ElectrolyteType
parameters.description: Binary11LiquidElectrolyte (default Lithium-Ion Battery) or SingleIonConductor.

parameters.name: prop("CellSettings") CellSOCandInitialChargeInventory
parameters.description: Enable the SOC and Initial Charge Distribution node.

parameters.name: Electrolyte conductivity
parameters.description: Effective ionic conductivity of the solid electrolyte.

tools.notes: Settings for the electrolyte salt concentration are disabled in all nodes when this option is used. The Java type of the Lithium-Ion Battery interface is LithiumIonBatteryMPH (not LithiumIonBattery).

tools.name: Lithium-Ion Battery, Deformed Geometry (Model Wizard entry)
tools.description: Predefined multiphysics entry that adds a Lithium-Ion Battery interface, a Deformed Geometry interface, and Deforming Electrode Surface and Nondeforming Boundary couplings. The mesh moves with the deposition/dissolution velocity of electrode reactions, for example lithium metal plating and stripping at a lithium-metal negative electrode.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Batteries > Lithium-Ion Battery, Deformed Geometry; couplings Java types: "DeformingElectrodeSurfaceDeformedGeometry", "NonDeformingBoundaryDeformedGeometry"

parameters.name: Deforming Electrode Surface
parameters.description: Boundaries whose normal velocity equals the total deposition velocity.

parameters.name: Nondeforming Boundary
parameters.description: Boundaries kept fixed (or sliding) in the deformed geometry.

parameters.name: Dissolving-depositing species
parameters.description: Molar mass and density of lithium metal on the Electrode Surface.

tools.notes: An existing battery model can be extended manually by adding Deformed Geometry plus the two coupling nodes. Use automatic remeshing for large deformations.

tools.name: Battery with Binary Electrolyte (batbe)
tools.description: Battery interface for cells with an alkaline aqueous binary (1:1) electrolyte such as NiMH, NiCd or Zn/AgO, using concentrated electrolyte theory for charge and mass transport and Ohm's law in electrodes. Porous electrodes can contain intercalating particles solved in an extra dimension, several electrode materials, film resistance and adsorption/desorption reactions. Solves phil, phis, cl and particle concentration cs.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Batteries > Battery with Binary Electrolyte; Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("batbe", "BatteryBinaryElectrolyte", "geom1")

parameters.name: prop("BatBeSpecies") McatPlus, ManMinus, M0
parameters.description: Molar masses of cation, anion and solvent (e.g. K+, OH-, H2O).

parameters.name: Porous Electrode / Particle Intercalation
parameters.description: Electrode volume fractions, particle radius, diffusivity, maximum concentration.

parameters.name: Insertion Reaction kinetics
parameters.description: Porous Electrode Reaction kinetics type for NiMH main reactions.

parameters.name: Electrolyte solution density
parameters.description: Default 1293 kg/m^3 (KOH).

tools.notes: Variables batbe.cs_surface, batbe.cs_center and batbe.cs_average give particle concentrations.

tools.name: Lead-Acid Battery (leadbat)
tools.description: Battery interface for lead-acid cells: Ohm's law in the electrodes, concentrated electrolyte theory for sulfuric acid (H+/HSO4-), and porosity mass balances in the positive (PbO2) and negative (Pb) porous electrodes that track state of charge through lead sulfate formation. A cell typically has positive electrode, reservoir, separator and negative electrode domains.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Batteries > Lead-Acid Battery; Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("leadbat", "LeadAcidBattery", "geom1")

parameters.name: Negative / Positive Porous Electrode
parameters.description: Porosity at zero charge eps0, fully charged epsmax, porosity exponent exm, conductivity.

parameters.name: Reservoir
parameters.description: Free electrolyte with conductivity, salt diffusivity and optional volume-change-driven velocity.

parameters.name: Porous Electrode Reaction
parameters.description: Lead-acid battery charge/discharge kinetics types.

tools.notes: Default nodes: Reservoir, Electric Insulation, No Flux and Initial Values.

tools.name: Reservoir / Negative and Positive Porous Electrode (Lead-Acid Battery)
tools.description: Domain nodes of the Lead-Acid Battery interface. Reservoir defines current and salt balances in free electrolyte, with convection from volume changes of the negative or positive main reaction or a user velocity. Negative Porous Electrode (Pb) and Positive Porous Electrode (PbO2) set up electrode and pore-electrolyte current balances, salt balance and porosity balance; the porosities at zero and full charge define the capacity and soc variable.
tools.usage: Lead-Acid Battery > Reservoir / Negative Porous Electrode (npe1) / Positive Porous Electrode (ppe1); Java types: "Reservoir", "NegativePorousElectrode", "PositivePorousElectrode"

parameters.name: sigmal, Dl
parameters.description: Electrolyte conductivity and salt diffusivity.

parameters.name: eps0, epsmax
parameters.description: Porosity at zero charge and when fully charged.

parameters.name: exm
parameters.description: Exponent on porosity for effective transport.

parameters.name: Mean surface-averaged velocity
parameters.description: From negative or positive main reaction, or user defined.

tools.notes: Add Porous Electrode Reaction subnodes with the lead-acid charge/discharge kinetics.

tools.name: Lumped Battery (lb)
tools.description: Black-box battery interface based on a small set of lumped parameters: cell capacity, initial SOC, open-circuit voltage versus SOC, and ohmic, activation and concentration (diffusion) overpotentials, optionally with double-layer capacitance. Operation modes are galvanostatic, potentiostatic, power, charge-discharge cycling, circuit terminal and load cycle; heat sources are computed for thermal coupling. Works in 0D or on domains (global or local variables) for thermal models and packs.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Batteries > Lumped Battery; Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("lb", "LumpedBattery") (0D) or create("lb", "LumpedBattery", "geom1")

parameters.name: prop("BatterySettings") OperationMode
parameters.description: Galvanostatic (I_app), Potentiostatic (E_app), Power, ChargeDischargeCycling, CircuitTerminal or LoadCycle.

parameters.name: LumpedBatModel
parameters.description: LumpedCell or TwoElectrodes.

parameters.name: Q_cell0, SOC_cell0
parameters.description: Initial cell capacity and initial state of charge.

parameters.name: Cell Equilibrium Potential / Voltage Losses
parameters.description: Default subnodes with OCV data and loss parameters.

tools.notes: Result variables include lb.E_cell, lb.I_cell and lb.SOC_cell; 1C current lb.I_1C_cell.

tools.name: Lumped Battery, Two Electrodes (single-particle lumped model)
tools.description: Model Wizard entry of Lumped Battery using the Two electrodes model: lumped charge-transfer and diffusion parameters are defined separately for the negative and positive electrodes, solving individual degrees of conversion, which corresponds to a single-particle model in the literature. Initial charge distribution is set by cell SOC or voltage with the total charge inventory from host capacities, and formation loss can be included. Electrode-specific aging nodes (charge inventory and host capacity loss) are available.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Battery Interfaces > Lumped Battery, Two Electrodes; Java: model.component("comp1").physics("lb").prop("BatterySettings").set("LumpedBatModel", "TwoElectrodes")

parameters.name: Q_host_neg0, Q_host_pos0
parameters.description: Initial negative and positive host capacities.

parameters.name: Cell voltages at 0% and 100% SOC
parameters.description: From operational potential limits or user defined.

parameters.name: Negative/Positive Equilibrium Potential
parameters.description: Electrode OCP vs degree of conversion (from material or user function).

parameters.name: Voltage Losses: J0_neg, J0_pos, tau_neg, tau_pos
parameters.description: Per-electrode exchange current and diffusion time constants.

tools.notes: In COMSOL 6.4 the documentation lists no separate Single Particle Battery interface; single-particle models are built with this option or with Thin Porous Electrode nodes in Lithium-Ion Battery (SPM/SPMe).

tools.name: Cell Equilibrium Potential (Lumped Battery)
tools.description: Default subnode of the Lumped cell model defining battery thermodynamics: the open-circuit voltage at a reference temperature and its temperature derivative versus SOC (local tables, user functions or from definitions), or alternatively OCV and thermoneutral voltage as functions of SOC and temperature. The data drive the cell voltage and the reversible (entropic) heat.
tools.usage: Lumped Battery > Cell Equilibrium Potential (cep1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("lb").feature("cep1").set("OpenCircuitVoltageInput", "fromdef")

parameters.name: OpenCircuitVoltageInput
parameters.description: Local table, user defined, or fromdef (use a function from Definitions).

parameters.name: Eocvdef / dEocvdTdef
parameters.description: Functions for OCV and dOCV/dT when fromdef is used.

parameters.name: SOC_Eocv, Eocv
parameters.description: Local table columns of SOC and OCV.

tools.notes: Local tables use linear interpolation and extrapolation. Also used under Battery Pack > Batteries.

tools.name: Voltage Losses (Lumped Battery)
tools.description: Default subnode defining voltage losses under load: ohmic overpotential scaled from its value at 1C, optional activation overpotential from a dimensionless exchange current J0 (about 25 mV at 1C for J0 = 1) with optional double-layer capacitance, and optional concentration overpotential from a particle diffusion model with diffusion time constant tau or a resistor-capacitor pair. The Two electrodes model uses separate negative and positive activation and diffusion parameters.
tools.usage: Lumped Battery > Voltage Losses (vl1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("lb").feature("vl1").set("eta_ir1C", "eta_IR_1C")

parameters.name: eta_ir1C
parameters.description: Ohmic overpotential at 1C.

parameters.name: J0 (J0_neg, J0_pos)
parameters.description: Dimensionless charge exchange current.

parameters.name: IncludeConcentrationOverpotential, tau
parameters.description: Diffusion-related loss and its time constant.

parameters.name: Include double-layer capacitance
parameters.description: Capacitive charging for fast transients (lumped cell).

tools.notes: Parameters can be temperature dependent, e.g. J0_0*Arrh(Ea, T), when coupled to heat transfer.

tools.name: Capacity Loss (Lumped Battery)
tools.description: Aging subnode of the Lumped cell model that computes capacity fade from a loss current of parasitic reactions. The built-in kinetics use a calendar aging time constant multiplied by optional aging factors for voltage (offset potential, transfer coefficient), current (cycling capacity loss factor), aging history (decelerating factor) and temperature (Arrhenius activation energy); a user-defined loss current is also possible. Used for calendar and cycle life studies.
tools.usage: Lumped Battery > Capacity Loss (cl1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("lb").create("cl1", "CapacityLoss", -1)

parameters.name: tau_loss
parameters.description: Calendar aging time constant.

parameters.name: factorE, E_offset, alpha
parameters.description: Voltage-dependent aging factor.

parameters.name: factorI, H
parameters.description: Current (cycling) aging factor.

parameters.name: factoraged, G
parameters.description: Aging-history (decelerating) factor.

parameters.name: Temperature factor
parameters.description: Activation energy and reference temperature.

tools.notes: A cycling factor of 2e-4 with other factors equal to 1 adds about 20% capacity loss after 1000 full cycles.

tools.name: Charge Inventory Loss / Host Capacity Loss (Lumped Battery, Two Electrodes)
tools.description: Aging subnodes of the Two electrodes lumped model: Negative and Positive Charge Inventory Loss reduce the cyclable charge (for example SEI growth consuming lithium), while Negative and Positive Host Capacity Loss reduce the active host material of each electrode. Each uses built-in loss kinetics (calendar time constant with voltage, current, history and temperature factors) or a user-defined loss current.
tools.usage: Lumped Battery (Two electrodes) > Negative/Positive Charge Inventory Loss, Negative/Positive Host Capacity Loss

parameters.name: Loss kinetics
parameters.description: Built in or User defined loss current per electrode.

parameters.name: Calendar aging time constant
parameters.description: Base rate of parasitic reactions.

parameters.name: Aging factors
parameters.description: Voltage, current, aging history and temperature dependencies.

tools.example:
1. Set LumpedBatModel = TwoElectrodes on the Lumped Battery interface.
2. Add Negative Charge Inventory Loss with a calendar aging time constant and a temperature factor.
3. Run a long Time Dependent study with a repeating Load Cycle and plot the remaining capacity and lb.SOC_cell.
tools.notes: Also available under Battery Pack > Batteries when the Two electrodes model is used.

tools.name: Short Circuit (Lumped Battery)
tools.description: Subnode that adds an internal short-circuit conductance to a lumped battery, giving short-circuit currents and the corresponding heat source. It models self-discharge or internal short scenarios; in battery packs it can be triggered by thermal events.
tools.usage: Lumped Battery > Short Circuit (isc1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("lb").create("isc1", "ShortCircuit", -1)

parameters.name: G_short
parameters.description: Short-circuit conductance (S).

tools.notes: The property name G_short follows the documented symbol; the Battery Pack thermal event uses G_short_te.

tools.name: Battery Equivalent Circuit (Model Wizard entry)
tools.description: Model Wizard entry that creates an Electrical Circuit interface prepopulated with elements for an equivalent-circuit battery model: a Battery Open Circuit Voltage source depending on SOC, the load current and an internal resistance, extendable with Resistor-Capacitor Couples, capacitors and inductors. Used to monitor SOC and voltage response during load cycles or for system-level simulation.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Batteries > Battery Equivalent Circuit; Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("cir", "Circuit"); physics("cir").create("OCV1", "BatteryOpenCircuitVoltage"); create("RC1", "ResistorCapacitorCouple")

parameters.name: Battery Open Circuit Voltage
parameters.description: OCV vs SOC, battery capacity and initial SOC.

parameters.name: Resistor-Capacitor Couple
parameters.description: RC pair representing diffusion/charge-transfer dynamics.

parameters.name: Current Source / Resistor
parameters.description: Load current and series resistance.

tools.notes: Parameters are typically fitted with Parameter Estimation to pulse test data.

tools.name: Battery Pack (bp)
tools.description: 3D interface that defines many lumped battery cells at once and connects them electrically. Default nodes are Batteries (one lumped or two-electrode cell model per disjoint domain group), Current Conductors (busbars, connectors), and Negative and Positive Connectors between cells and conductors; the pack load is applied on conductor boundaries. Heat sources couple to heat transfer via Electrochemical Heating for thermal management and runaway propagation studies.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Batteries > Battery Pack (3D only); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("bp", "BatteryPack", "geom1")

parameters.name: Batteries
parameters.description: Cell model (LumpedCell/TwoElectrodes), capacity, initial SOC, OCV and voltage losses shared by all cells or from materials.

parameters.name: Current Conductors / Thin Current Conductors
parameters.description: Electric conductivity (and thickness) of wiring.

parameters.name: Negative/Positive Connectors
parameters.description: Cell-to-conductor connection boundaries with optional contact resistance.

parameters.name: Pack load
parameters.description: Electrode Current, Charge-Discharge Cycling or Load Cycle on conductor boundaries.

tools.notes: Result variables such as bp.E_cell_max/avg/min, bp.SOC_max/avg/min, bp.T_cell_<n> summarize individual cells.

tools.name: Batteries (Battery Pack)
tools.description: Default domain node of Battery Pack defining one battery cell model per disjoint group of selected domains, using the Lumped cell or Two electrodes formulation of Lumped Battery. Default subnodes are Cell Equilibrium Potential (or Negative/Positive Equilibrium Potential) and Voltage Losses; Thermal Event, capacity-loss and Short Circuit subnodes can be added. Specify battery properties from materials allows cell-to-cell parameter variation.
tools.usage: Battery Pack > Batteries (batt); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("bp").feature("batt").set("LumpedBatModel", "LumpedCell")

parameters.name: LumpedBatModel
parameters.description: LumpedCell or TwoElectrodes.

parameters.name: Q_cell0, SOC_cell0 / SOC_pack0
parameters.description: Cell capacity and initial SOC.

parameters.name: InputsFromMaterials
parameters.description: Take cell parameters from assigned materials.

parameters.name: InitialChargeType, E_cell0
parameters.description: Initial state from SOC or cell voltage.

tools.notes: Subnodes Cell Equilibrium Potential and Voltage Losses are singletons locked to the Batteries selection.

tools.name: Thermal Event (Battery Pack, thermal runaway)
tools.description: Subnode of Batteries that adds an event-triggered heat source to cells for thermal runaway propagation studies. The event fires once per cell when the maximum or average cell temperature exceeds a trigger temperature or at an explicit time; the heat source after the event is a function of elapsed time (local table, user expression or function). The event can also add ohmic overpotential or an internal short-circuit conductance.
tools.usage: Battery Pack > Batteries > Thermal Event (te1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("bp").feature("batt").create("te1", "ThermalEvent", 3)

parameters.name: EventConditionType
parameters.description: Maximum cell temperature, average cell temperature (maxT_te, avgT_te) or ExplicitTime (t_exp).

parameters.name: HeatSourceAfterEventType, t_te_tab, Qh_te_tab
parameters.description: Heat source versus time after the event.

parameters.name: AddOhmicOverPotentialAfterEvent, eta_ir1C_te
parameters.description: Extra internal resistance after the event.

parameters.name: AddShortCircuitAfterEvent, G_short_te
parameters.description: Short-circuit conductance after the event.

tools.notes: Several Thermal Event nodes can represent different decomposition reactions. Couple to Heat Transfer via Electrochemical Heating (ECHeat_physics = bp).

tools.name: Current Conductors / Thin Current Conductors (Battery Pack)
tools.description: Battery Pack nodes defining the electrical wiring of the pack. Current Conductors are domains (busbars, serial and parallel connectors, terminals) with an electric conductivity; Thin Current Conductors are boundaries with a thickness and conductivity, avoiding meshing of thin foils. Both carry Initial Values and Insulation subnodes and host the pack load boundary conditions.
tools.usage: Battery Pack > Current Conductors (ccnd) / Thin Current Conductors

parameters.name: Electric conductivity
parameters.description: Conductivity of the conductor material.

parameters.name: Current conductor thickness
parameters.description: Thickness of thin conductors.

parameters.name: Boundary subnodes
parameters.description: Electric Ground, Electrode Current, Charge-Discharge Cycling, Load Cycle.

tools.example:
Application Library: Battery_Design_Module/Thermal_Management/battery_pack_6s2p.
1. Keep the default Current Conductors node on the busbar domains.
2. Add Ground and Current subnodes on the pack terminals and set the pack current.
tools.notes: Current is exchanged with the cells only through Negative/Positive Connectors.

tools.name: Negative / Positive Connectors (Battery Pack)
tools.description: Default boundary nodes of Battery Pack that define where each cell's negative or positive terminal connects to the current conductor domains. Each cell's current is set implicitly by potential constraints at these boundaries; an optional contact resistance can be included.
tools.usage: Battery Pack > Negative Connectors (nc) / Positive Connectors (pc); Java types: "NegativeConnectors", "PositiveConnectors"

parameters.name: IncludeContactResistance, Rc
parameters.description: Contact resistance (ohm*m^2).

tools.notes: Selections must be the interfaces between battery domains and conductor domains.

tools.name: Porous Electrode (Lithium-Ion Battery)
tools.description: Domain node of the battery interfaces combining current balances in the porous electrode matrix and pore electrolyte, the electrolyte salt balance, and (with Intercalating particles) the solid-phase lithium balance in a Particle Intercalation subnode. It holds electrolyte and electrode material links, volume fractions, tortuosities and Bruggeman-type effective-transport corrections, dissolving-depositing species with volume-fraction updates, and film resistance for SEI modelling.
tools.usage: Lithium-Ion Battery > Porous Electrode (pce1) > Particle Intercalation (pin1), Porous Electrode Reaction (per1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("liion").create("pce1", "PorousElectrode", 1)

parameters.name: epss, epsl
parameters.description: Electrode and electrolyte volume fractions.

parameters.name: ElectrolyteMaterial / ElectrodeMaterial
parameters.description: Materials for electrolyte and electrode properties.

parameters.name: IonicCorrModel, DiffusionCorrModel, ElectricCorrModel (fl, fDl, fs)
parameters.description: Bruggeman, tortuosity, user-defined or no correction.

parameters.name: IntercalationOption
parameters.description: IntercalatingParticles or NonIntercalatingParticles.

parameters.name: Species / FilmResistanceType
parameters.description: Dissolving-depositing species and film resistance.

tools.notes: The solid concentration variable is liion.cs_pce1; averages liion.cs_average, liion.cs_surface and the degree of lithiation liion.soc_average_pce1.

tools.name: Particle Intercalation (Lithium-Ion Battery)
tools.description: Subnode of Porous Electrode and Additional Porous Electrode Material that solves diffusion of intercalated lithium in electrode particles in an extra (pseudo) dimension, as in the pseudo-2D Newman/DFN model. It sets the initial concentration (or initial electrode potential), maximum concentration, particle type (spheres, cylinders, flakes) and radius, transport model (Fick's law, Baker-Verbrugge, or no spatial gradients), particle mesh, operational potential limits, and optional particle-resolved heat of mixing.
tools.usage: Porous Electrode > Particle Intercalation (pin1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("liion").feature("pce1").feature("pin1").set("rp", "rp_neg")

parameters.name: ParticleMaterial
parameters.description: Material providing Ds, csmax and equilibrium data.

parameters.name: csinit
parameters.description: Initial intercalated concentration (or Einit with equilibrium concentration function).

parameters.name: rp
parameters.description: Particle mean center-surface distance (radius).

parameters.name: Ds_mat / Ds
parameters.description: Intercalation diffusivity (user defined allows concentration dependence via liion.cs_pce1).

parameters.name: Distribution, Nel, FastAssembly
parameters.description: Particle-dimension mesh distribution, number of elements, fast assembly.

parameters.name: HeatMix
parameters.description: Particle-resolved heat of mixing and power losses.

tools.notes: With SOC and Initial Charge Distribution active, the initial concentration is computed from the cell SOC. Results in the particle dimension are plotted with atxd1/atxd2/atxd3 operators.

tools.name: Porous Electrode Reaction, Lithium Insertion (Lithium-Ion Battery)
tools.description: Porous Electrode subnode for the intercalation charge-transfer reaction. Besides general kinetics, battery interfaces provide Lithium Insertion kinetics (Butler-Volmer form depending on electrolyte, surface and maximum solid concentrations via a reference exchange current density i0,ref(T) or rate constant), Insertion Reaction for binary-electrolyte batteries and lead-acid charge/discharge kinetics. Extra subnodes model side reactions such as SEI formation or lithium plating.
tools.usage: Porous Electrode > Porous Electrode Reaction (per1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("liion").feature("pce1").feature("per1").set("i0_ref", "i0ref_neg")

parameters.name: MaterialOption
parameters.description: Material providing Eeq and dEeq/dT (e.g. mat2 graphite).

parameters.name: ElectrodeKinetics
parameters.description: LithiumInsertion (default), ButlerVolmer, ConcentrationDependentKinetics, etc.

parameters.name: i0_ref / k
parameters.description: Reference exchange current density or rate constant.

parameters.name: Eeq_mat, dEeqdT_mat
parameters.description: Equilibrium potential and temperature derivative source.

parameters.name: av
parameters.description: Active specific surface area (particle-based by default).

tools.notes: Several Porous Electrode Reaction subnodes on one electrode model self-discharge or capacity fade reactions.

tools.name: Additional Porous Electrode Material (Lithium-Ion Battery)
tools.description: Domain node applied on top of an active Porous Electrode to add a second active material (blended electrodes such as LMO+NMC or graphite+silicon) or a second particle size, each with its own volume fraction, Particle Intercalation and Porous Electrode Reaction subnodes. Its currents enter the parent electrode's electrolyte and electrode balances.
tools.usage: Lithium-Ion Battery > Additional Porous Electrode Material (addm1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("liion").create("addm1", "IntercalatingMaterial", 1)

parameters.name: epssadd
parameters.description: Volume fraction of the additional material.

parameters.name: IntercalationOption
parameters.description: Intercalating or non-intercalating particles.

parameters.name: Particle Intercalation / Porous Electrode Reaction subnodes
parameters.description: Material-specific diffusion and kinetics.

tools.notes: Java type is IntercalatingMaterial; Thin Additional Porous Electrode Material is the boundary variant for Thin Porous Electrode.

tools.name: Particle Size Distribution / Multiple Particle Sizes (Lithium-Ion Battery)
tools.description: Approaches for electrodes with heterogeneous particle sizes. The straightforward way is several Additional Porous Electrode Material nodes, one per size class; for large ensembles the Application Library tutorial introduces an extra particle-size dimension using auxiliary dependent variables and weak contributions, with state variables for particle measures from a histogram.
tools.usage: Lithium-Ion Battery > Additional Porous Electrode Material (per size class), or Auxiliary Dependent Variable + Weak Contribution nodes for a continuous size distribution

parameters.name: Size classes
parameters.description: Radius and volume fraction per class.

parameters.name: Auxiliary Dependent Variable / Weak Contribution
parameters.description: Advanced features used to add a size dimension (AuxiliaryField, WeakContribution).

tools.example:
Application Library: Battery_Design_Module/Lithium-Ion_Batteries,_Performance/particle_size_distribution.
1. Start from the 1D DFN model.
2. Add one Additional Porous Electrode Material per size class with rp = r_i and epssadd = eps_i.
3. Compare discharge curves with the single-size model.
tools.notes: Multiple materials also increase the number of extra-dimension unknowns; use FastAssembly in 1D models.

tools.name: Thin Porous Electrode (single-particle SPM/SPMe)
tools.description: Boundary node on exterior boundaries of an electrolyte or separator domain representing a thin porous electrode with thickness and electrode volume fraction, optional intercalating particles and a default Porous Electrode Reaction. It neglects gradients through the electrode thickness, so combining it with a single separator domain gives a single-particle model with electrolyte (SPMe), or with the single-ion conductor option a classic SPM.
tools.usage: Lithium-Ion Battery > Electrolyte submenu > Thin Porous Electrode (tpce1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("liion").create("tpce1", "ThinPorousElectrode", 0)

parameters.name: d_pe
parameters.description: Thickness of the thin electrode.

parameters.name: epss
parameters.description: Electrode volume fraction.

parameters.name: IntercalationOption
parameters.description: Intercalating particles (adds Particle Intercalation).

parameters.name: BoundaryCondition
parameters.description: Electrode phase potential condition (electric potential, current, load cycle...).

tools.notes: Valid for low-to-medium currents and thin or highly conductive electrodes; widely used for aging, pack and parameter-estimation studies.

tools.name: Porous Conductive Binder (Lithium-Ion Battery)
tools.description: Domain node for electrochemically inactive but electronically conductive porous regions, such as the carbon-binder domain in particle-resolved (heterogeneous) electrode models. It solves electrolyte and electrode current balances with effective-transport corrections and can host Nonfaradaic Reactions, Porous Matrix Double-Layer Capacitance and dissolving-depositing species.
tools.usage: Lithium-Ion Battery > Porous Conductive Binder (pcb1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("liion").create("pcb1", "PorousConductiveBinder", 3)

parameters.name: epss, epsl
parameters.description: Volume fractions of conductive phase and electrolyte.

parameters.name: Effective transport correction
parameters.description: Bruggeman or user-defined corrections.

tools.notes: Resolved active particles are modelled with Transport in Solids and Internal Electrode Surface nodes using Lithium Insertion kinetics (see heterogeneous_lib).

tools.name: Electrolyte / Separator (Lithium-Ion Battery)
tools.description: Domain nodes for the electrolyte phase of battery interfaces. Electrolyte defines free electrolyte with conductivity, salt diffusion coefficient, transport number (default 0.363) and activity dependence, plus velocity when convection is on; Separator adds a porous electronically insulating matrix with volume fraction and effective-transport corrections. Material library electrolytes (e.g. LiPF6 in EC:DMC) provide temperature- and concentration-dependent data.
tools.usage: Lithium-Ion Battery > Electrolyte (ice1) / Separator (sep1, default); Java types: "Electrolyte", "Separator"

parameters.name: sigmal, Dl, transpNum, fcl
parameters.description: Conductivity, diffusivity, transport number, activity dependence.

parameters.name: epsl, correction models
parameters.description: Separator porosity and Bruggeman-type corrections.

parameters.name: Solution density
parameters.description: Binary-electrolyte battery interface only.

tools.notes: Electrolyte does not represent pore electrolyte in porous electrodes (use Porous Electrode).

tools.name: Reaction Source (Lithium-Ion Battery)
tools.description: Advanced domain node that adds sources or sinks to the electrolyte salt mass balance, for example from chemical decomposition reactions of the electrolyte or cation-releasing side reactions. It is found under Additional Sources when Advanced Physics Options are shown.
tools.usage: Show Advanced Physics Options > Lithium-Ion Battery > Additional Sources > Reaction Source (rs1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("liion").create("rs1", "ReactionSource", 1)

parameters.name: Salt source
parameters.description: Source term for the electrolyte salt (mol/(m^3*s)).

tools.example:
Application Library: Battery_Design_Module/Lithium-Ion_Batteries,_Aging_and_Abuse/lmo_decomposition (manganese dissolution with cation net chemical reactions).
model.component("comp1").physics("liion").create("rs1", "ReactionSource", 1);
tools.notes: Combine with Transport of Diluted Species for other dissolved species (Porous Electrode Coupling).

tools.name: Porous Matrix Adsorption/Desorption Reaction (Battery with Binary Electrolyte)
tools.description: Porous Electrode subnode for nonfaradaic reactions on particle surfaces, for example hydrogen adsorption and desorption in NiMH batteries. The rate expression k (mol/(m^2*s)) and stoichiometric coefficient of the intercalating species define a surface source for the particle mass balance.
tools.usage: Battery with Binary Electrolyte > Porous Electrode > Porous Matrix Adsorption/Desorption Reaction

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Surface reaction rate expression (mol/(m^2*s)).

parameters.name: vs
parameters.description: Stoichiometric coefficient of the intercalating species.

parameters.name: av
parameters.description: Active specific surface area (postprocessing of volumetric source).

tools.notes: Also available under Additional Porous Electrode Material and Thin Porous Electrode in batbe.

tools.name: SOC and Initial Charge Distribution (Lithium-Ion Battery)
tools.description: Global node activated by Define cell state of charge (SOC) and initial charge inventory on the interface. It computes cell capacity, SOC, SOH and the 1C current, and sets the initial state by cell voltage, cell SOC, electrode potentials or charge inventories, for full or half cells. Child nodes Negative/Positive Electrode Domain (or Boundary) Selection must cover the Particle Intercalation nodes of each electrode.
tools.usage: Lithium-Ion Battery > SOC and Initial Charge Distribution (socicd1) with Negative/Positive Electrode Domain Selection; Java: model.component("comp1").physics("liion").prop("CellSettings").set("CellSOCandInitialChargeInventory", true)

parameters.name: InitialChargeType
parameters.description: CellSOC, CellVoltage, electrode potentials or charge inventories.

parameters.name: SOC_init / Ecell_init
parameters.description: Initial cell SOC or voltage.

parameters.name: Ecell_0SOC, Ecell_100SOC, CellVoltageInputType
parameters.description: Cell voltages defining 0% and 100% SOC.

parameters.name: CellType
parameters.description: FullCell or HalfCell (with reference counter-electrode potential).

tools.notes: Defines liion.SOC_cell, liion.SOH_cell, liion.I_1C_cell and the cell capacity; enables C Rate load-cycle steps and C-rate multiples in current conditions.

tools.name: Electrode Reaction: Lithium Metal / Insertion Reaction (Lithium-Ion Battery)
tools.description: Electrode Reaction kinetics options specific to the Lithium-Ion Battery interface on Electrode Surface or Internal Electrode Surface boundaries. Lithium metal describes lithium deposition and dissolution at a lithium-metal electrode (half cells, lithium-metal batteries); Insertion Reaction describes intercalation on boundaries of resolved particles in heterogeneous (particle-resolved) electrode models.
tools.usage: Lithium-Ion Battery > Electrode Surface (es1) > Electrode Reaction (er1) > Kinetics expression type = Lithium metal | Insertion reaction; Java: feature("es1").feature("er1").set("ElectrodeKinetics", "LithiumMetal")

parameters.name: ElectrodeKinetics
parameters.description: LithiumMetal or InsertionReaction (plus general types).

parameters.name: i0_ref
parameters.description: Reference exchange current density.

parameters.name: Dissolving-depositing species
parameters.description: Lithium metal molar mass and density for thickness change.

tools.notes: Couple with the Lithium-Ion Battery, Deformed Geometry entry to move the lithium surface.

tools.name: Charge-Discharge Cycling (battery boundary condition)
tools.description: Boundary condition for CC-CV cycling: each cycle starts with constant discharging or charging current until the minimum or maximum voltage is reached, optionally followed by constant-voltage periods ending at lower/upper cutoff currents and by rest periods. Currents can be explicit or C-rate multiples when SOC is defined. A cycle counter variable (e.g. liion.cdc1.cycle_counter) can drive stop conditions.
tools.usage: Lithium-Ion Battery (or other electrochemistry interface) > Charge-Discharge Cycling (cdc1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("liion").create("cdc1", "ChargeDischargeCycling", 0)

parameters.name: StartWith
parameters.description: Charge_first or Discharge_first.

parameters.name: ChargingCurrentType / Crate_ch / Ich
parameters.description: Charging current as C-rate multiple or explicit value (same for discharging).

parameters.name: Vmax, Vmin
parameters.description: Voltage limits ending the constant-current periods.

parameters.name: item.CVCH, item.CVDCH, iupper, ilower
parameters.description: Include constant-voltage charging/discharging and cutoff currents.

parameters.name: item.OCCH, item.OCDCH, trech, tredch
parameters.description: Include rest periods and their durations.

tools.notes: Apply on the positive current collector. Cell voltage and current are available as liion.cdc1.phis0 and liion.cdc1.Icell. For arbitrary protocols use Load Cycle.

tools.name: C Rate / Power / Subloop (Load Cycle subnodes)
tools.description: Additional Load Cycle child nodes in battery interfaces. C Rate sets a dimensionless C-rate (Lumped Battery, or Lithium-Ion Battery with SOC defined), Power sets a power in W (potentiostatic-and-galvanostatic load type), and Subloop repeats its child nodes until an elapsed-time, completed-cycles or user-defined break condition is met (up to three nested levels). Values can be constants, functions or step sequences, with the same continuation conditions as Current/Voltage/Rest.
tools.usage: Load Cycle > C Rate (crate1) / Power / Subloop (subl1); Java types: "CRate", "Subloop"

parameters.name: setVal / InputType
parameters.description: C-rate or power value, function or step sequence.

parameters.name: TimeCondition, tmax / voltage limits
parameters.description: Continuation conditions.

parameters.name: Subloop break conditions
parameters.description: Elapsed subloop time, number of completed cycles, user condition.

tools.notes: Subloop is not available when Use elapsed time only is enabled on the Load Cycle.

tools.name: SEI Layer Growth and Capacity Fade (Lithium-Ion Battery aging)
tools.description: Modelling approach from the Application Library for solid-electrolyte-interphase growth on graphite: a second Porous Electrode Reaction on the negative electrode represents the parasitic lithium/solvent reduction (user-defined local current I_SEI), a dissolving-depositing species 'sei' tracks the film, its volume reduces the electrolyte volume fraction, and the Porous Electrode film resistance (thickness and conductivity) adds the SEI potential drop. Charge-discharge cycling then yields irreversible loss of cyclable lithium and capacity fade.
tools.usage: Lithium-Ion Battery > Porous Electrode (negative) > Dissolving-Depositing Species + Film Resistance + additional Porous Electrode Reaction

parameters.name: Species = sei
parameters.description: Dissolving-depositing SEI species with molar mass and density.

parameters.name: FilmResistanceType = ThicknessAndConductivity, sf0, sigmaf
parameters.description: Initial SEI thickness and conductivity.

parameters.name: per2: ilocmat = I_SEI, Vib
parameters.description: Side-reaction current density and stoichiometry.

tools.notes: The seed model sei_formation_seed contains the battery without SEI. For lumped aging use the Lumped Battery Capacity Loss node.

tools.name: Lithium Plating and Stripping (Lithium-Ion Battery)
tools.description: Modelling approach for lithium plating on graphite during fast charging or at low temperature: lithium metal and dead lithium are dissolving-depositing species in the negative Porous Electrode, and an extra Porous Electrode Reaction with concentration-dependent kinetics represents plating and stripping (Eeq = 0 V vs Li/Li+). A fraction Ydead of stripped lithium becomes electrically isolated, giving irreversible capacity loss predicted versus C-rate and temperature.
tools.usage: Lithium-Ion Battery > Porous Electrode (negative) > Species LiMetal, LiDead + Porous Electrode Reaction (ConcentrationDependentKinetics)

parameters.name: Species LiMetal, LiDead
parameters.description: Dissolving-depositing species for plated and dead lithium.

parameters.name: ElectrodeKinetics = ConcentrationDependentKinetics, i0, CR
parameters.description: Plating kinetics with coverage-limited stripping.

parameters.name: Vib
parameters.description: Stoichiometry splitting stripped lithium into active and dead lithium (Ydead).

tools.notes: Plating current variable liion.iloc_per2 can be monitored to design fast-charging protocols (see lib_charge_rate_optimization).

tools.name: Battery Heat Sources and Thermal Coupling (liion.Qh, Electrochemical Heating)
tools.description: Battery interfaces compute the total heat source liion.Qh (lb, bp and batbe equivalents) from Joule heating, activation losses, reversible entropic heat (dEeq/dT) and optionally heat of mixing. It is passed to Heat Transfer by the Electrochemical Heating coupling, or averaged from a 1D electrochemical model into a 2D/3D thermal model through model inputs and nonlocal couplings (one-way or two-way coupled). Temperature-dependent parameters then follow the thermal solution.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Electrochemical Heating (ECHeat_physics = liion/lb/bp, Heat_physics = ht), or Heat Transfer > Heat Source Q = aveop1(comp1.liion.Qh) in a coupled 1D-3D setup

parameters.name: liion.Qh
parameters.description: Total electrochemical heat source (W/m^3).

parameters.name: dEeqdT_mat / dEeqdT
parameters.description: Entropic coefficient for reversible heat.

parameters.name: HeatMix / UseApproximateHeatOfMixing
parameters.description: Heat of mixing options.

tools.notes: Lithium-Ion Battery, Lumped Battery and Battery Pack all define heat sources usable by Electrochemical Heating.

tools.name: Battery Result Variables (SOC, cell voltage, capacity, lithiation)
tools.description: Common battery result variables: liion.SOC_cell, liion.SOH_cell, liion.I_1C_cell and liion.Q_cell (cell capacity) from the SOC node; electrode lithiation liion.soc_average_pce1 and local surface lithiation liion.socloc_surface; cell voltage and current from boundary conditions such as liion.lc1.E_app, liion.lc1.I_app, liion.cdc1.phis0, liion.cdc1.Icell, liion.phis0_ec1; Lumped Battery lb.E_cell, lb.I_cell, lb.SOC_cell; Battery Pack bp.E_cell_max/avg/min, bp.SOC_max/avg/min and per-cell bp.T_cell_<n>, bp.E_cell_<n>.
tools.usage: Results > Global Evaluation / 1D Plot Group > Global with expressions such as liion.SOC_cell

parameters.name: liion.cs_surface / cs_average / cs_center
parameters.description: Particle concentrations in the real dimension.

parameters.name: liion.cdc1.cycle_counter
parameters.description: Cycle counter of Charge-Discharge Cycling.

tools.notes: Variable names depend on feature tags (lc1, cdc1, ec1, pce1).

tools.name: Diffusion-Induced Stress (Lithium-Ion Battery + Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Application approach coupling intercalation to particle mechanics: the particle concentration from the Lithium-Ion Battery model drives a concentration-induced (hygroscopic-swelling-like) strain in a Solid Mechanics model of a representative particle, giving radial, tangential and von Mises stresses during discharge and relaxation. Stress is highest at the particle surface during delithiation and relaxes with concentration gradients.
tools.usage: Lithium-Ion Battery (1D cell) + Solid Mechanics on a particle geometry, coupled through the particle concentration from the extra dimension

parameters.name: Partial molar volume
parameters.description: Links concentration change to volumetric strain.

parameters.name: Particle concentration
parameters.description: Taken from liion.cs_pce1 at a chosen cell position.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics Module for the solid mechanics part. Particle-resolved (heterogeneous) models can also couple mechanics directly.

tools.name: Parameter Estimation for Battery Models
tools.description: The Battery Design Module includes the Parameter Estimation study node with BOBYQA, IPOPT and Levenberg-Marquardt solvers, even without an Optimization Module license, to fit unknown parameters (diffusivities, rate constants, lumped resistances, time constants) to measured voltage or impedance data in stationary or time-dependent models.
tools.usage: Study > Parameter Estimation (lsqo) with Global Least-Squares Objective / experimental data; Java: model.study("std1").create("lsqo", "LSQOptimization")

parameters.name: Estimated parameters
parameters.description: Parameter names, initial values, scales and bounds.

parameters.name: Experimental data
parameters.description: Time/voltage columns mapped to model expressions.

parameters.name: Optimization method
parameters.description: Levenberg-Marquardt, BOBYQA or IPOPT.

tools.notes: Documentation of the node is in the Optimization Module User's Guide shipped with the Battery Design Module.
